name: Bank purchase of USD against documented current-account income, then one outward wire (foreign individual, 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 59)
who: A non-Chinese individual who earned lawful current-account RMB in China and still holds documents showing the income and the tax
governing: Art. 59, 汇发〔2020〕14号 (C03); Art. 5 and Art. 12, 国务院令第532号 (C06)
documents: Passport; source-of-funds documents showing the transaction amount, including tax evidence (税务凭证); the bank's own FX-purchase form
ceiling: No amount limit in the text; above USD 50,000 per day the bank requires the documents (C22)
pros: The mainstream, documented route: the bank prices the conversion and wires the dollars; a full paper trail; no quota to wait for
cons: Only available for money the documents support; the bank reviews purpose consistency; the spread and the wire fee are unavoidable; Chinese tax on the income must be settled first
step1: Take the passport, the income documents and the Chinese tax evidence to the bank that holds the account.
step2: The bank reviews the documents against the source of funds and the stated purpose (Art. 12, C06).
step3: Instruct the purchase of USD and the outward wire in the same visit; the bank applies its board selling rate (C01) plus the tariff (C02).
step4: Keep the bank's FX-purchase form and the wire confirmation: these are the U.S. basis evidence for the currency gain (C11).

name: One outward wire from foreign currency already held in a PRC FX account
who: Anyone with USD (or other FX) already sitting in a Chinese foreign-currency account
governing: Art. 64, 汇发〔2020〕14号 (C22); SAFE 2006 individual FX rules (inherited register)
documents: Passport; for amounts above USD 50,000 per day, documents showing the transaction amount (C22)
ceiling: USD 50,000 per day on ID alone; above that with documents (C22)
pros: No conversion spread at all - the money is already in dollars; only the wire fee applies
cons: Only works if the balance is already foreign currency; most stuck balances are RMB, which needs M01, M04, M05 or M06 first
step1: Confirm with the bank that the account is a foreign-currency account and the balance is USD.
step2: Instruct the outward wire; the bank charges the tariff (C02).
step3: Above USD 50,000 per day, supply the transaction documents the bank asks for (C22).

name: Cross-border RMB remittance: send CNY out and convert to USD offshore
who: Account holders whose bank supports cross-border RMB business; depends on the bank and on the payee
governing: PBOC cross-border RMB arrangements (inherited register S24); Art. 5 and Art. 12, 国务院令第532号 (C06)
documents: Passport; bank-specific cross-border RMB forms; a receiving account able to accept CNY
ceiling: Bank-specific; no official figure read in this pass
pros: If available, the RMB leaves as RMB and the conversion happens outside China's FX-purchase rules
cons: The conversion cost then depends entirely on the offshore bank or platform, and THIS SESSION VERIFIED NO FIGURE for that conversion - the row is left blank
step1: Ask the Chinese bank whether it will remit CNY to a named offshore account (this varies by bank and by branch).
step2: Ask the receiving bank or platform for its CNY-to-USD price in writing before sending anything.
step3: Send a small test amount and compare the landed dollars with the mid-market rate.
step4: Only then send the balance. The spread is UNVERIFIED in this edition and is flagged.

name: Annual convenience amount (USD 50,000 a year) - only for a holder of a Chinese Foreign Permanent Resident ID
who: A foreign national holding a PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID card; NOT available to a US citizen travelling on a passport alone
governing: Arts. 55-56, 汇发〔2020〕14号 (C04); for domestic individuals only (C05)
documents: The Foreign Permanent Resident ID card
ceiling: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year as a convenience amount; still not a cap, but the ID alone will not carry more (C05)
pros: Eight calendar years of ID-only conversions if the card is held; no documents per transfer
cons: A US citizen without the card cannot use it at all; eight years of exposure to the rate and to rule changes; eight wire fees
step1: Check the wording on the card: 外国人永久居留身份证. Without it this route is closed.
step2: Convert and wire up to USD 50,000 equivalent per calendar year.
step3: Repeat in later calendar years; do not let anyone else use their quota for you (Art. 39/45, C06).

name: Emigrant property transfer (移民财产转移) - after giving up Chinese household registration and emigrating
who: A person who emigrated from China and is transferring property acquired before leaving
governing: 汇发〔2024〕12号 6.4 as quoted by SAFE Tianjin (C09); PBOC 2004 No.16 (inherited register)
documents: Application to the SAFE branch at the former household-registration place; identity, emigration and property documents; tax evidence
ceiling: No official ceiling read in this pass; approval is by the SAFE branch (C09)
pros: A formal route for a large pre-emigration balance, approved once and then remitted
cons: Only for emigrants with pre-emigration property; requires SAFE approval at the former registration place; documents must prove the source; timeline not published
step1: Confirm that you emigrated from China and that the money is pre-emigration property.
step2: Apply to the SAFE branch at your former household-registration place (C09).
step3: After approval, buy FX and remit through the bank, keeping the approval and the tax evidence.
step4: This route was NOT tested by this session - the approval timeline and any fee are blank and flagged.

name: Inheritance property transfer (继承财产转移)
who: An heir to a PRC-registered deceased person
governing: 汇发〔2024〕12号 6.4 as quoted by SAFE Tianjin (C09)
documents: Application to the SAFE branch where the deceased was registered; inheritance documents; tax evidence
ceiling: No official ceiling read in this pass
pros: The formal route for inherited money, including money that would otherwise have no documented source
cons: Requires a death, an inheritance right and probate-type documents; approval timeline not published
step1: Obtain the inheritance documents and the deceased's registration details.
step2: Apply to the SAFE branch where the deceased was registered (C09).
step3: After approval, buy FX and remit, keeping all approvals.

name: Sale proceeds of PRC real property you own, remitted with the registered contract and the tax certificate
governing: Art. 5 and Art. 12, 国务院令第532号 (C06); inherited register routes L04/S15
documents: Registered sale contract; property-title documents; the PRC tax payment certificate for the sale
ceiling: No official ceiling read in this pass
pros: A large, documented, one-off sum that the bank can verify
cons: PRC tax on the gain must be paid first; the sale must be real and registered; THIS SESSION DID NOT RE-READ the property-tax rule, so the rate here is UNVERIFIED and blank
step1: Complete a registered sale and pay the PRC taxes due on it.
step2: Take the contract, the title documents and the tax certificate to the bank.
step3: Buy FX and wire in one instruction.

name: Dividend or profit distribution from a PRC company you own, then one outward wire
who: An owner of a PRC company with distributable profits
governing: Art. 22 and Art. 23, 国务院令第532号 (C06); C08 for the tax filing above USD 50,000
documents: Board/shareholder resolution; audited accounts; PRC tax payment evidence (withholding); the tax filing above USD 50,000 (C08)
ceiling: No official ceiling read in this pass
pros: Turns company profit into personal dollars lawfully with a clean paper trail
cons: The company must have after-tax profit; PRC withholding applies first (I14 shows 20% only as an illustration and was NOT re-read); the tax filing adds a step
step1: Distribute after resolving the company's PRC taxes.
step2: File the outbound-payment tax record if the payment exceeds USD 50,000 (C08).
step3: Buy FX and wire with the resolution and the tax evidence.

name: Service-trade payment against a genuine service contract (for work you actually performed)
who: A person or business with a real cross-border service contract
governing: C08 (tax filing); Art. 12, 国务院令第532号 (C06)
documents: The signed contract; invoices; tax evidence; the tax filing above USD 50,000 (C08)
ceiling: No official ceiling read in this pass
pros: A documented current-account channel with a clear audit trail
cons: Only lawful if the service is real; inventing an invoice is the offence in Art. 40 (C06)
step1: Have a real contract and real invoices.
step2: Complete the tax filing if above USD 50,000 (C08).
step3: Buy FX and wire with the contract.

name: UnionPay / bank-card cash withdrawal abroad from a mainland debit card
who: Holder of a mainland-issued debit card
governing: 汇发〔2017〕29号 (C07); BOC ATM tariff (C19 - NOT re-read by this session)
ceiling: CNY 100,000 equivalent per person per calendar year across all cards; CNY 10,000 equivalent per card per day (C07)
pros: Fast, no bank visit, small amounts only
cons: Hard annual ceiling of CNY 100,000 (about USD 15,000) - cannot move USD 400,000; every withdrawal costs a fee and a cash rate; exceeding the cap suspends the card abroad for that year and the next (C07)
step1: Confirm the annual CNY 100,000 limit has not been used up.
step2: Withdraw at most CNY 10,000 equivalent per card per day.
step3: Record the fee per withdrawal; the ATM tariff C19 was not re-read this pass, so the fee column here is BLANK and flagged.

name: Carrying foreign-currency banknotes out of China in person
governing: Art. 15 and Art. 42, 国务院令第532号 (C06); inherited register R15 (SAFE Hebei Q&A)
documents: Passport; a bank-issued carrying permit above USD 5,000 and up to USD 10,000; a SAFE permit above USD 10,000
ceiling: USD 5,000 without a permit; up to USD 10,000 with a bank permit; above USD 10,000 a SAFE permit, in principle not granted (inherited R15 - not re-read this session)
pros: Physical dollars in hand; no wire fee
cons: A USD 400,000 balance would be 80 permitted trips at USD 5,000; carrying more than USD 10,000 into the U.S. requires a FinCEN 105 report (C18); the cash rate applies and loss/theft risk is yours; no official source supports using this for a large balance
step1: Buy foreign cash at the bank and obtain the carrying permit above USD 5,000.
step2: Declare on FinCEN Form 105 if the amount entering or leaving the U.S. exceeds USD 10,000 (C18).
step3: Repeat - which is why this route is impractical above a few thousand dollars.

name: Change unused RMB back with the original exchange slip
who: Someone who previously bought RMB with foreign currency and still holds the original slip
governing: inherited register route L02/S09 (SAFE Q&A); not re-read by this session
documents: The original FX-purchase slip (兑换水单) plus passport
ceiling: Limited to the amount originally exchanged, per the inherited text - NOT re-read this session
pros: Reverses an earlier conversion with minimal documentation
cons: Only works for money that came in from abroad and was converted, and only within the slip's limits; the governing Q&A was NOT re-read this session, so this row is flagged
step2: Ask the bank to reconvert within the amount and time the slip allows.

name: Keep the RMB balance in China and spend it from there (do nothing now)
who: Anyone not forced to move the money today
governing: Art. 5, 国务院令第532号 (C06); the FBAR and 8938 duties apply annually regardless (C16)
documents: None to move; annual FBAR if the aggregate exceeds USD 10,000 (C16)
pros: Zero conversion cost today; no PRC tax event; you keep optionality and can wait for a better rate
cons: The U.S. reporting duties continue every year (FBAR, and Form 8938 above the threshold); the balance stays exposed to the exchange rate; a future rule change is out of your hands
step1: File the FBAR each year the aggregate exceeds USD 10,000 (C16).
step3: Revisit the conversion when the documents or the rate justify it.

name: Split the amount across relatives' or friends' annual convenience amounts (分拆, "ant moving")
who: Anyone tempted to use other people's quotas
governing: Art. 39 (逃汇) and Art. 45, 国务院令第532号 (C06); SAFE watch-list practice (inherited register)
pros: None that survives the risk: it is the offence the rules are written to stop
cons: Fine up to 30% of the amount (30-100% in serious cases) plus possible criminal liability (C06); the counterparties are exposed too
step2: If a bank or agent proposes it, decline in writing.
step3: Use M01, M05, M06 or M07 instead.

name: Private currency exchange, money changers, underground banks, or swapping with another person
who: Anyone offered a "better rate" outside a bank
pros: None lawful: the advertised rate is the price of the illegality
cons: Warning, confiscation of gains and a fine up to 30% of the amount (30-100% serious), plus criminal liability (C06); counterparty risk is total - no legal recourse
step2: Treat any offer of an off-board rate as a red flag.
step3: Compare the lawful costs in the cost tables instead.

name: Buy cryptocurrency or a stablecoin with RMB in China and sell it abroad for USD
governing: 银发〔2026〕42号 (C10), which repeals and replaces 银发〔2021〕237号
pros: None lawful: the activity itself is designated an illegal financial activity
cons: Converting legal tender to virtual currency inside China, or virtual currency to virtual currency, is an illegal financial activity that is strictly prohibited and suppressed (C10); banks and payment institutions may not service it; losses are the investor's own under the notice
step2: Note that the 2026 notice replaced the 2021 one and kept the prohibition.

name: False invoices, false purpose, or an undisclosed excess of cash
who: Anyone offered "purpose packaging" by an agent
governing: Art. 40 (非法套汇) and Art. 42, 国务院令第532号 (C06); C18 for U.S. cash reporting
cons: The conversion is reversed, a fine of up to 30% (30-100% serious) applies and criminal liability is possible (C06); an unreported USD 10,000-plus cash entry can be seized (C18)
step2: Keep every document genuine and consistent between the FX purchase and the payment (Art. 12, C06).
